House Financial Services Committee press release, 2025-07-30
grade_reason: Hill speaks about AI often as Financial Services Committee chairman, but only as an innovation and regulation issue for the financial sector; nothing found acknowledges or dismisses catastrophic risk. Both quoted statements are from 2025; no 2026 statement in his own words on AI was found.
notes: Nine web searches ran; none was refused. Search was otherwise thin on 2026 material. A search summary attributed to Hill the words "when it comes to artificial intelligence, we need smart safeguards in place to protect consumers, prevent abuse, and ensure our families and financial systems are safe", but I could not find its source or date (a follow-up search found nothing), so it is left out. At a 2026-02-04 hearing Hill asked Treasury Secretary Bessent about AI in customer service and compliance (FedScoop, https://fedscoop.com/treasury-department-artificial-intelligence-banking-industry/), but the article only paraphrases him. The March 26, 2026 committee hearing on regulators and technology contained no AI remarks by Hill in the summary I read. His hill.house.gov press release index (June to October 2026) showed no AI releases in its excerpts. The 'opportunity, not a threat' quote: PYMNTS splits the sentence with an attribution; the quoted passage is the continuous second part. It could be read as mildly dismissive of AI threats, but it names no catastrophic risk, so I graded it D, not F. No source shows Hill co-sponsored the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act (H.R. 10538, lead sponsor Rep. Greg Casar; reported cosponsors are Democrats), but I did not open the congress.gov cosponsor list. He was a member of the 2024 House Bipartisan Task Force on AI (before the 2025 window).
